title: Minimum Testable Iteration Decision Tree
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Entrepreneurship
description: A vertical decision tree with three yes/no diamonds, one each for service before product, manual before automated, and pre-selling before building. For Jordan's grooming van or Priya's meal-prep subscription, learners choose between a sound answer and a common founder objection at each diamond. Judgments that hold add a design note to the tree; objections light an amber Reconsider branch with an explanation. After three judgments, the card shows the combined minimum testable iteration, and the tree keeps the path that justifies it.

prerequisites: Chapter 6: Designing the Solution & Initial Offer
Chapter 10 reading through Three Rules for a Lean Test
educational.topic: Designing a minimum testable iteration with service before product, manual before automated, and pre-selling before building
learningObjectives: Given a venture scenario, evaluate which lean-test principles (service before product, manual before automated, pre-selling before building) apply, and justify a resulting minimum testable iteration design

controls.label: Yes / No answer (two per diamond, each with its reasoning)
controls.purpose: Judge whether the current principle applies; a judgment that holds adds a design note and opens the next diamond, one that does not hold lights the Reconsider branch with feedback

controls.label: Scenario
controls.purpose: Switch between Jordan's grooming van and Priya's meal-prep subscription; switching starts the new path at the first diamond

controls.label: Reset
controls.purpose: Return to the first diamond and clear the reconsider count

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Judgment at each decision node with immediate explanatory feedback, keeping the full decision path visible as the justification for the final design
keyQuestions: Can this be delivered as a hands-on service before it's a packaged product?
Can this be delivered by hand, without new software or equipment?
Can a customer pay something before the full offer exists?
Which part of the final design does each principle justify?
commonMisconceptions: The packaged product, such as a grooming van or a leased kitchen, has to exist before anyone can be served
Software or an app is needed before the first few customers can book
Asking for money before the full offer exists is unfair, so the first test should be free
A free trial or a stated interest shows demand as well as a payment does
assessmentOpportunities: Explain why a founder objection such as the van has to come first does not hold
Write a three-part minimum testable iteration for a new venture and justify each part with its principle
Explain why a deposit is stronger evidence than a free trial or a stated interest
